card.title: SLASHERS
card.text: When a friendly unit survives combat, add a GARRISON unit to your support line.
card.flavorText: The Gloucestershire Regiment, nicknamed Glosters or Slashers, was an infantry regiment of the British Army active between 1881 and 1994. At the outbreak of WWII the regiment was composed of four battalions (1st, 2nd, 5th and 7th), but later the 10th Battalion was added. The 2nd and 5th Battalions were deployed in France as part of the British Expeditionary Force, and both participated in the Battle of France before retreating to Dunkirk, where they were evacuated. In 1942 the 1st Battalion saw action in Burma, where it provided rearguard for the British retreat from Rangoon during the Japanese conquest of Burma. After heavy losses the battalion was sent to India to rest and recuperate, and it spent the remainder of the war there. In 1944 the 2nd Battalion participated in the Normandy landings and fought in the Battle of Normandy as part of the 56th Independent Infantry Brigade. From there it advanced into Belgium and the Netherlands, and ended the war in Germany where some of the men served as guards during the Nuremberg trials. The 10th Battalion of the Gloucestershire Regiment, assigned to the 72nd Brigade in the 36th Infantry Division, also fought in Burma. Despite lacking jungle warfare training, they engaged in key battles such as the relief of the Admin Box, the capture of Mayu tunnels, and the fierce fighting at Pinwe. The battalion faced significant losses, particularly from sickness and combat, losing many officers during intense engagements. After a controversial battle at Myitsone in February 1945, which led to the dismissal of their commanding officer, the battalion reached Mandalay, then returned to India in May, and was disbanded in December 1945.
